newsitem.title: CANADA: Bloc Quebecois regains some Quebec support - polls.
newsitem.headline: Bloc Quebecois regains some Quebec support - polls.

text.p: The separatist Bloc Quebecois is regaining some of the support it lost in Quebec earlier in the campaign for the June 2 federal election, according to two polls published on Thursday.

A SOM Inc poll in the Montreal daily newspaper La Presse showed support for the Bloc at 35 percent, compared with 33 percent for Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals and 28 percent for the Conservatives. The results included a proportional distribution of the 19 percent undecided vote.
The survey showed the Bloc gaining four points from a poll taken a week earlier, La Presse said.
The poll, which was conducted May 23-27 among 1,002 Quebec voters, had a 3.7 percent margin of error 19 times out of 20.

A CROP poll published in Quebec City's Le Soleil and broadcast on the TVA network showed the Bloc with 36 percent support, versus 32 percent for the Liberals and 28 percent for the Conservatives, after distribution of the 19 percent undecided vote.
A May 17-22 poll showed Bloc support at 35 percent, Le Soleil said.
The CROP poll was conducted May 22-26 among 1,007 Quebec voters and had a 3 percent margin of error 19 times out of 20.
Le Soleil said the CROP poll showed a high degree of voter volatility as 41 percent of respondents said their choice of party could change.

CROP spokesman Claude Gauthier said any vote exchange would likely occur between the Conservatives and the Bloc as 50 percent of those supporting the Conservatives said they could change their vote, versus 35 percent for the Bloc.
